# CoDa Stereo

> **Compositional Data Analysis for Stereological, Histomorphometric and
> Blood-Cell Data**
>
> A Shiny application implementing the Aitchison geometry for the full
> data analysis cycle: data upload, zero/NA handling, compositional
> visualisation, balances, and permutational MANOVA with post-hoc tests.
> Interface in English, Portuguese and Spanish.
>
> Developed alongside: Provete, D.B., Severgnini, M.R., Fernandes, C.E.
> & Franco-Belussi, L. *A Practical Guide to using Compositional Data
> Analysis in Tissue Stereology and Blood Cell Profile*. **Physiological
> Reports** (in review).

**Use it online, no installation needed:**
<https://sxzbf8.short.gy/CoDaStereo> (the interface opens in English;
add `?lang=pt` or `?lang=es` to the link for Portuguese or Spanish).

See [NEWS.md](https://provetelab.org/CoDaStereo/NEWS.md) for the changes
in each version and the [package
website](https://provetelab.org/CoDaStereo/) for the getting-started
guide.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Features

| Module | Capabilities |
|----|----|
| **Data Upload** | CSV and Excel (.xlsx/.xls) with sheet selector; the four case-study datasets of the companion paper as examples; aggregation of fields of view into specimens (nested designs); smart parts selector; pre-flight check |
| **Data Inspection** | Zero/NA heatmap (observed vs. structural zero vs. missing); [`naniar::vis_miss`](https://docs.ropensci.org/visdat/reference/vis_miss.html) plot; counts per part |
| **Zero Handling** | Three methods via `zCompositions`: CZM (count zeros), multRepl (rounded zeros), lrEM (rounded zeros); NA handling via listwise deletion or geometric-mean imputation |
| **Compositional Analysis** | Ternary plot in pure ggplot2 with amalgamation, convex hulls or 95% confidence/predictive regions and group centres; clr-biplot on unscaled clr coordinates (axis choice, shapes, labels, optional log-total as in a T-space biplot) with a “how to read” note, scree plot and ray lengths; variation-matrix heatmap; compositional centre and total variance per group; colour palettes (Okabe-Ito, Dark2, viridis); interactive hover (`ggiraph`) |
| **Balances (SBP)** | Automatic sequential binary partition (Ward clustering on clr distances), editable cell by cell with on-the-fly validation; CoDa dendrogram; boxplots and permutational tests (Z, P) of each balance by group |
| **Statistical Modeling** | Permutational MANOVA via [`RRPP::lm.rrpp`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/RRPP/man/lm.rrpp.html) with factors, covariates (ANCOVA), a block term, SS type I/II/III and 199-9999 permutations (fixed seed); the log-total as a joint response or a covariate (Pawlowsky-Glahn, Egozcue & Lovell 2015), with a warning when totals are fixed by design; pairwise tests of means and dispersions; residual diagnostics. Fits run in background workers (`mirai`) |
| **Reproducibility** | R script that reproduces the analysis; self-contained HTML report; save and reload the session (JSON) |
| **Downloads** | Every figure as PDF, PNG, SVG or TIFF at a chosen size, resolution and font size; imputed data, SBP, variation matrix, ANOVA, balance and pairwise tables as CSV |

## Installation

### Run locally

Install the binary package from
[r-universe](https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev/CoDaStereo) (no build
tools needed):

``` r

install.packages("CoDaStereo",
  repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# Launch
CoDaStereo::run_app()
```

Or install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("diogoprov/CoDaStereo")
```

### Run without installing (quick start)

``` r

# Clone the repo, then:
setwd("CoDaStereo/")
pkgload::load_all()
run_app()
```

### Dependencies

CoDaStereo depends on: `shiny`, `shinydashboard`, `rintrojs`, `dplyr`,
`tidyr`, `tibble`, `purrr`, `ggplot2`, `ggiraph`, `ggrepel`, `scales`,
`svglite`, `readxl`, `naniar`, `compositions`, `zCompositions`, `RRPP`,
`FactoMineR`, `mirai`, `htmltools`, `jsonlite`, `knitr`, `golem`,
`rlang`.

All are available on CRAN.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Deploy to Posit Connect Cloud (free)

Connect Cloud is Posit’s next-generation hosting platform. It deploys
directly from a public GitHub repository with automatic push-to-publish.

### Step-by-step

1.  **Fork or push this repository** to your GitHub account.

2.  **Generate `manifest.json`** — this file tells Connect Cloud which R
    version and packages to use. Run this once in your local R session
    (from the repository root):

    ``` r

    # install.packages("rsconnect")
    # list only the files the deployed app needs
    f <- system("git ls-files", intern = TRUE)
    f <- f[grepl("^(app[.]R|DESCRIPTION|NAMESPACE|LICENSE|R/|www/|inst/)", f)]
    rsconnect::writeManifest(appDir = ".", appFiles = f, appPrimaryDoc = "app.R")
    # (the same code is in dev/write_manifest.R)
    ```

    Commit and push the generated `manifest.json`.

3.  **Sign in to [Connect Cloud](https://connect.posit.cloud/)** with
    your GitHub account.

4.  **Click “Publish”** (+ icon at the top), select your repository and
    branch (`main`). Connect Cloud will detect `app.R` and deploy
    automatically.

5.  **Get a shareable URL** — share it in your manuscript or
    supplementary materials.

### Updating the app

After the initial setup, every `git push` to `main` triggers an
automatic re-deploy. No manual steps needed.

### Alternative: deploy from RStudio

``` r

# One-time authentication (opens browser)
rsconnect::connectCloudUser()

# Deploy
rsconnect::deployApp(appDir = ".", appName = "CoDaStereo")
```

## Repository structure

    CoDaStereo/
    ├── app.R                  # Entry point for Posit Connect Cloud
    ├── DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, LICENSE, NEWS.md, _pkgdown.yml
    ├── manifest.json          # Generated by rsconnect::writeManifest()
    ├── R/
    │   ├── run_app.R          # golem entry point: run_app()
    │   ├── app_ui.R           # Dashboard layout (assembles modules)
    │   ├── app_server.R       # Wires modules, session state and restore
    │   ├── fct_helpers.R      # Zeros, ternary plot, palettes, SBP, total, clr-PCA, examples
    │   ├── fct_plots.R        # Biplot, scree, variation matrix, regions, balances, export
    │   ├── fct_models.R       # RRPP model fitting and background workers (mirai)
    │   ├── fct_reproducibility.R  # R script, HTML report, session JSON
    │   ├── fct_i18n.R         # English / Portuguese interface
    │   ├── mod_data.R         # Upload, examples, specimen aggregation, inspection
    │   ├── mod_imputation.R   # Zero/NA imputation
    │   ├── mod_analysis.R     # Ternary, biplot, variation matrix, descriptives
    │   ├── mod_balances.R     # SBP editor, CoDa dendrogram, balance tests
    │   ├── mod_stats.R        # MANOVA, pairwise tests, diagnostics
    │   ├── mod_export.R       # Reproducibility tab
    │   └── mod_tutorial.R     # Guided tour (rintrojs)
    ├── inst/extdata/          # Case-study example datasets
    ├── inst/i18n/             # Portuguese translations (UTF-8)
    ├── inst/logo/             # Hex sticker (SVG, PNG)
    ├── tests/testthat/        # Unit, module and reproducibility tests
    ├── vignettes/             # Getting started
    ├── data-raw/              # Scripts that build the examples and translations
    ├── dev/                   # Development scripts (run_dev.R, write_manifest.R)
    └── .github/workflows/     # R CMD check (3 OSes) and pkgdown site

## Why “CoDa Stereo”?

The name joins the two fields that the package brings together: *CoDa*,
the usual abbreviation of compositional data analysis, and *stereology*,
the quantification of tissue structure whose volume fractions and point
counts are compositions by construction. It is also a double musical
homage.
[*Coda*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coda_(Led_Zeppelin_album)) (1982)
is the ninth and final studio album by Led Zeppelin, released almost two
years after the band broke up following the death of drummer John
Bonham, and its title refers to the closing section of a piece of music.
[Soda Stereo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soda_Stereo) is the band
formed in Buenos Aires in 1982 by Gustavo Cerati, Zeta Bosio and Charly
Alberti, regarded as a pioneer of Latin American rock. Changing a single
letter turns Soda Stereo into CoDa Stereo.

The logo carries both references in its typography. “CODA” is set in
[Ryga](https://justfreefonts.com/fonts/ryga/), a free display typeface
with neon-like outlined strokes, chosen as a homage to Led Zeppelin’s
*Coda*. “STEREO” is set in Inter Bold, widely spaced, as a solid 1980s
nod to Soda Stereo. Above the name, an isometric block of tissue with
cells and blood vessels stands for the object of stereology, and its
stacked bars stand both for the parts of a composition and for the level
meters of a stereo equalizer. The package has no connection with either
band, and the logo uses none of their artwork or lyrics. The fonts are
documented in
[`inst/logo/FONTS.md`](https://provetelab.org/CoDaStereo/inst/logo/FONTS.md).

## How to cite

If you use CoDaStereo in your research, please cite both the paper and
the software:

``` bibtex
@article{provete2026codastreo,
  author  = {Provete, Diogo B. and Severgnini, Marcos R. and Fernandes, Carlos E. and Franco-Belussi, Lilian},
  title   = {A Practical Guide to using Compositional Data Analysis in Tissue Stereology and Blood Cell Profile},
  journal = {Physiological Reports},
  year    = {2026},
  note    = {In review}
}

@software{provete2026codastreo_app,
  author  = {Provete, Diogo B.},
  title   = {{CoDa Stereo}: Compositional Data Analysis for Stereological Data},
  year    = {2026},
  url     = {https://github.com/diogoprov/CoDaStereo},
  doi     = {10.5281/zenodo.19925778},
  version = {3.1.1}
}
```
